author: e. j. halstead
title: Little Rock Trojans lose to Oral Roberts, split midweek baseball series
text:
The Little Rock Trojans lost to Oral Roberts 11–1 at Gary Hogan Field on March 18, splitting their two-game midweek baseball series. Each team won one game by the same score.
The result ended Little Rock’s streak of three consecutive games with 12 or more hits, as the Golden Eagles held them to a season-low five hits. The Trojans now have an overall record of 11-10.
Head coach Chris Curry said, “I knew Oral Roberts would come in today and respond after getting run-ruled yesterday, and they jumped on us early. Our command was a bit elevated today, and offensively, we pulled a lot of pitches on the ground, and that’s not our approach. We were trying to pull the ball a bit too much.”
Curry also highlighted individual performances despite the loss: “Josh Beezley got us out of a jam with the bases loaded. Preston Davis was really good for us today, and he’s a guy we can use in high-leverage situations because of his stuff. Both of those guys are high-leverage arms. There were some bright spots on offense, too: Kade Smith with two hits, David Stanley off the bench, and Lance Anderson filled in nicely at shortstop.”
Nic Bronzini started for Little Rock and took the loss as one of eight pitchers used during the game. Offensively, Nolan Freund doubled while Ty Rhoades drove in the team’s only run with a sacrifice fly. Anderson added a single alongside Smith’s two-hit performance; Stanley contributed a pinch-hit single in the eighth inning.
Looking ahead, Little Rock will travel to Cookeville, Tennessee to open Ohio Valley Conference play against Tennessee Tech this weekend. The series begins Friday at 6 p.m., with Saturday and Sunday games scheduled for 2 p.m. and 1 p.m., respectively. All three games will be available on ESPN+.
